newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Advance says ASC not to take action.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Advance says ASC not to take action.

text.p: Advance Bank Australia Ltd chairman Jim Service said the Australian Securities Commission would not block the bank's use of a deeming proxy provision to proceed with its merger with St George Bank Ltd.

"This morning a representative of the Australian Securities Commission phoned and said that the Commission had decided to appear at the court hearing on January 6 but it would not be opposing our use of this mechanism," Service said, adding the ASC would be making some comments before the Supreme Court.
Service also said he understood that National Australia Bank Ltd had abstained from voting at Monday's meeting.
NAB has a stake of about three percent in Advance.

Ahead of today's meeting of Advance shareholders, where they overwhelmingly approved the merger, there was speculation that NAB would act somehow to block the combination of the two Sydney-based regionals.

The ASC said last Friday it had some concerns about the proxy method, where abstaining votes were counted in favour of the merger proposal. The regulator indicated it could take some action when the scheme of arrangement of Advance was brought before the New South Wales Supreme Court for approval on January 6. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
